step.consistency.calculated: HCO₃⁻ was not entered and is calculated with Henderson–Hasselbalch: HCO₃⁻ = 0.0307 × pCO₂ × 10^(pH − 6.1).
step.consistency.check: [H⁺] from pH = 10^(9 − pH) is compared with [H⁺] = 24 × pCO₂ / HCO₃⁻. A discrepancy above 10% means a sampling or entry error.
step.ph.acidemia: pH below the age-specific normal range — acidaemia.
step.ph.alkalemia: pH above the age-specific normal range — alkalaemia.
step.ph.normal: pH is normal, but steps 3–6 are still performed: a hidden mixed disorder is possible.
step.primary.metabolic_acidosis: Acidaemia with low HCO₃⁻ — primary metabolic acidosis.
step.primary.metabolic_alkalosis: Alkalaemia with high HCO₃⁻ — primary metabolic alkalosis.
step.primary.respiratory_acidosis: Acidaemia with high pCO₂ — primary respiratory acidosis.
step.primary.respiratory_alkalosis: Alkalaemia with low pCO₂ — primary respiratory alkalosis.
step.primary.mixed_acidosis: pCO₂ is high and HCO₃⁻ is low at the same time — mixed (respiratory + metabolic) acidosis.
step.primary.mixed_alkalosis: pCO₂ is low and HCO₃⁻ is high at the same time — mixed (respiratory + metabolic) alkalosis.
step.primary.none: pH, pCO₂ and HCO₃⁻ are within normal limits — no acid–base disorder detected.
step.compensation.none: No primary disorder — compensation is not assessed.
step.compensation.metabolic_acidosis: Winters' formula: expected pCO₂ = 1.5 × HCO₃⁻ + 8 (±2). Higher — concomitant respiratory acidosis; lower — respiratory alkalosis.
step.compensation.metabolic_alkalosis: Expected pCO₂ = 0.7 × HCO₃⁻ + 21 (±2), not above 55. Higher — concomitant respiratory acidosis; lower — respiratory alkalosis.
step.compensation.respiratory_acidosis: Expected HCO₃⁻: acute = 24 + 0.1 × (pCO₂ − 40), chronic = 24 + 0.35 × (pCO₂ − 40), tolerance ±2. Above chronic — + metabolic alkalosis; below acute — + metabolic acidosis.
step.compensation.respiratory_alkalosis: Expected HCO₃⁻: acute = 24 − 0.2 × (40 − pCO₂), chronic = 24 − 0.4 × (40 − pCO₂), tolerance ±2. Below chronic — + metabolic acidosis; above acute — + metabolic alkalosis.
step.anionGap.insufficient: Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are required (and K⁺ in “AG with K⁺” mode).
step.anionGap.result: AG = Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻); AG_corr = AG + 0.25 × (40 − albumin, g/L). Elevation is judged by AG_corr.
step.deltaRatio.notApplicable: Calculated only when AG_corr is elevated and HCO₃⁻ < 24.
step.deltaRatio.normal_ag: Δ/Δ < 0.4 — hyperchloraemic normal anion gap acidosis.
step.deltaRatio.mixed_ag: Δ/Δ 0.4–0.8 — combined high and normal anion gap acidosis.
step.deltaRatio.pure_high_ag: Δ/Δ 0.8–2.0 — high anion gap acidosis without a second metabolic disorder (lactic acidosis often ~1.6, ketoacidosis ~1).
step.deltaRatio.plus_met_alk: Δ/Δ > 2.0 — concomitant metabolic alkalosis or compensated chronic respiratory acidosis.
step.osmolar.insufficient: Measured osmolality, Na⁺, glucose and urea are required.
step.osmolar.result: Calculated osm = 2 × Na⁺ + glucose + urea. Gap = measured − calculated; > 10 — toxic alcohols or osmotically active substances.
step.stewart.insufficient: SBE, Na⁺, Cl⁻ and albumin are required; lactate if available.
step.stewart.result: SBE is partitioned into the Na–Cl, albumin, lactate and unmeasured anion effects. Unmeasured anions < −2 — ketones, toxins, renal failure.
step.oxygenation.insufficient: FiO₂ and pO₂ (arterial sample) or SpO₂ ≤ 97% are required.
step.oxygenation.arterial: PAO₂ = FiO₂ × (Patm − 47) − PaCO₂ / 0.8. A-a = PAO₂ − PaO₂; P/F = PaO₂ / FiO₂; OI = MAP × FiO₂ × 100 / PaO₂.
step.oxygenation.nonArterial: Not an arterial sample: PaO₂-based indices are not calculated; OSI and S/F remain.
delta.mixed_ag: 0.4–0.8: combined high and normal AG acidosis
delta.pure_high_ag: 0.8–2.0: high AG acidosis without a second metabolic disorder
flag.inconsistent_sample.text: Inconsistent sample: [H⁺] from pH {hMeasured} vs {hCalc} nmol/L from HCO₃⁻. Sampling or entry error — calculation continued with a warning.
flag.hypokalemia.text: K⁺ {K} mmol/L (2.5–2.9): moderate hypokalaemia — ECG, check Mg²⁺, IV correction.
flag.hyperkalemia.text: K⁺ {K} mmol/L (6.0–6.4): moderate hyperkalaemia — ECG, rule out a haemolysed sample.
flag.temperature.text: Temperature {t} °C: the analyser reports at 37 °C, consider correction.
flag.venous_sample.text: Venous sample: pH is 0.03–0.05 lower than arterial, pCO₂ 4–8 higher, HCO₃⁻ 1–2 higher. PaO₂, A-a, P/F, OI are not calculated.
flag.capillary_sample.text: Capillary sample: pH and pCO₂ approximate arterial values only with good perfusion and a warmed heel; pO₂ is not interpreted.
flag.cord_vein_sample.text: Umbilical vein: interpret alongside the artery.
flag.ga_missing.text: Enter the gestational age for a preterm infant.
flag.normal_ph_mixed.text: Normal pH with pCO₂ and HCO₃⁻ shifted in the same direction: opposing mixed disorder or full compensation (full compensation is rare — look for a second disorder).
flag.neonatal_compensation.text: Compensation formulas are validated in adults; in neonates they are approximate.
flag.ag_without_albumin.text: Albumin not entered: AG may be underestimated in hypoalbuminaemia.
flag.ag_masked_by_albumin.text: Raw AG is normal but albumin-corrected AG is elevated — without correction the high AG acidosis would be missed.
flag.hidden_hagma.text: AG_corr is elevated while HCO₃⁻ is not below normal — hidden high anion gap metabolic acidosis.
flag.osmolar_gap.text: Osmolar gap {gap} mOsm/kg (> 10): toxic alcohols or osmotically active substances.
flag.stewart_no_lactate.text: Lactate not entered: lactate effect taken as 0.
flag.unmeasured_anions.text: Unmeasured anions {uma} mmol/L (< −2): ketones, toxins, renal failure.
flag.pao2_not_interpretable.text: Not an arterial sample: PaO₂, A-a, P/F and OI are not assessed.
flag.aa_elevated.text: A-a gradient above the age-specific normal.
flag.berlin_peep.text: The Berlin ARDS classification applies with PEEP ≥ 5 cmH₂O.
flag.preterm_hyperoxia.text: Hyperoxia in a preterm infant (PaO₂ {PaO2} mmHg): reduce FiO₂ first.
flag.cord_pathological_acidemia.text: Cord: pH < 7.0 or BE ≤ −12 — pathological acidaemia.
flag.cord_hypothermia.text: pH ≤ 7.0 or BE ≤ −16 — check the criteria for therapeutic hypothermia.
flag.cord_swapped.text: The vein is “worse” than the artery — samples were probably swapped.
flag.bicarb_resp_acidosis.text: Respiratory acidosis or inadequate ventilation: bicarbonate will increase CO₂.
flag.bicarb_lactic.text: Lactic acidosis without extreme acidaemia (pH ≥ {pH}): treat the cause.
flag.bicarb_keto.text: Ketoacidosis without extreme acidaemia (pH ≥ {pH}): insulin and fluids.
flag.bicarb_hypernatremia.text: Hypernatraemia: sodium bicarbonate will worsen it.
flag.bicarb_hypocalcemia.text: Uncorrected hypocalcaemia: alkalinisation will lower ionised Ca²⁺.
flag.bicarb_preterm_ivh.text: Preterm infant: risk of intraventricular haemorrhage with rapid infusion of a hypertonic solution.
flag.bicarb_normal_ag.text: In normal AG acidosis, bicarbonate is considered primarily for bicarbonate loss (diarrhoea, renal tubular acidosis).
diff.check.urineAG: Urine AG = UNa + UK − UCl (negative → GI, positive → renal)

treat.vent.title: Ventilation correction by pCO₂ (conventional)
treat.vent.formula: Rate_new = Rate_current × pCO₂_current / pCO₂_target (constant tidal volume)
treat.vent.limits: Calculated rate is outside reasonable limits for age ({lo}–{hi}) — capped. Reconsider tidal volume and ventilation strategy.
treat.hfo.title: HFO and oxygenation — direction only
treat.hfo.lowerPCO2: To lower pCO₂ on HFO: increase amplitude (ΔP); if needed, lower the frequency (on HFO this increases CO₂ elimination).
treat.hfo.raisePCO2: To raise pCO₂ on HFO: decrease amplitude.
treat.hfo.oxygenation: To improve oxygenation: raise MAP (recruitment) or PEEP, then FiO₂; check lung volume on X-ray.
treat.hfo.hyperoxia: Hyperoxia in a preterm infant: reduce FiO₂ first.
treat.cause.title: By cause
treat.cause.lactate: Lactic acidosis: assess perfusion and the source rather than giving bicarbonate.
treat.cause.saline: Excess 0.9% saline: switch to balanced solutions.
treat.cause.chlorideAlkalosis: Chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis: replace Cl⁻ and K⁺.

q.chronicity: Step 4. Acute or chronic (or a second disorder)?
q.differential: Which test will narrow the differential first?
hint.consistency: [H⁺] = 10^(9 − pH); compare with 24 × pCO₂ / HCO₃⁻. Tolerance 10%.
hint.ph: Normal pH for this age category: {lo}–{hi}.
hint.primary: Acidaemia: what explains the shift — pCO₂ above normal or HCO₃⁻ below? Alkalaemia — the reverse.
hint.compensationMet: Compare actual pCO₂ with the expected value ±2.
hint.ag: AG = Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻); correction: + 0.25 × (40 − albumin, g/L).
hint.osmolar: Calculated osm = 2 × Na⁺ + glucose + urea; gap > 10 is elevated.
hint.differential: Which test separates the causes in the first differential group?
hint.stewart: Unmeas. anions = SBE − [(Na − Cl − 38) + 0.25 × (42 − albumin) − lactate].
hint.oxygenation.berlin: P/F = PaO₂ / FiO₂: ≤ 300 mild, ≤ 200 moderate, ≤ 100 severe.
hint.oxygenation.neo: OI = MAP × FiO₂ × 100 / PaO₂: > 25 — iNO, > 40 — ECMO.
hint.oxygenation.child: OI ≥ 16 (or OSI ≥ 12) — severe PARDS by PALICC-2.
hint.bicarb: Contraindications: resp. acidosis, lactic or ketoacidosis without extreme acidaemia, hypernatraemia, hypocalcaemia.

flag.preterm_hyperoxia_spo2.short: SpO₂ above target in a preterm infant
flag.preterm_hyperoxia_spo2.text: SpO₂ {SpO2}% on oxygen in a preterm infant: target {lo}–{hi}% (European Consensus on RDS 2022). Reduce FiO₂.
flag.ards_sf_mild.text: S/F ≤ 315 with SpO₂ ≤ 97%: mild ARDS by the 2023 global definition (if clinical criteria are met).
flag.ards_sf_moderate.text: S/F ≤ 235 with SpO₂ ≤ 97%: moderate ARDS by the 2023 global definition.
flag.ards_sf_severe.text: S/F ≤ 148 with SpO₂ ≤ 97%: severe ARDS by the 2023 global definition.
flag.cord_hypothermia_borderline.text: pH 7.01–7.15 or BE −10…−15.9: therapeutic hypothermia only with additional criteria (Apgar ≤ 5 at 10 min or ongoing resuscitation) and signs of encephalopathy.
flag.bicarb_neonatal_slow.text: Neonates: 4.2% only (0.5 mmol/mL), infused slowly over at least {min} min; not recommended routinely during resuscitation (ILCOR/NRP).
err.sampleType: Choose the sample type: the analyzer assumes arterial by default, which is not always true.
quick.intro: Fields follow the ABL analyzer screen. Enter moves to the next field. pH, pCO₂ and sample type are required.
quick.hco3Hint: cHCO₃⁻(P) is the actual bicarbonate (further down on the ABL), not the standard cHCO₃⁻(P,st). cBase(Ecf) = SBE. FiO₂ is optional: the detailed form has a pO₂(a)/FO₂(I) field.
flag.possibly_venous.text: pO₂ {pO2} mmHg with sO₂ < 80% in an “arterial” sample: check the sample type. If it really is arterial, this is marked hypoxaemia.
step.labs.title: 10. Haemoglobin, oximetry, electrolytes, metabolites
step.labs.result: Thresholds depend on age: Hb — WHO 2024 and transfusion thresholds (TOP, AABB 2023), K⁺ and Ca²⁺ — paediatric and adult protocols, glucose — BAPM/PES, lactate — SSC, bilirubin — Maisels 2012 / AAP 2022.
step.labs.insufficient: Enter ctHb, oximetry, K⁺, Ca²⁺, glucose, lactate or bilirubin.
flag.anemia.text: Hb {hb} g/L is below the age-specific limit ({lo} g/L, WHO 2024 / age norms).
flag.hb_transfusion.text: Hb {hb} g/L is below the restrictive threshold {thr} g/L (children — TAXI; adults — AABB 2023: 70, cardiac surgery 75, orthopaedic surgery or CVD 80).
flag.hb_transfusion_preterm.text: Hb {hb} g/L is below the restrictive TOP threshold {thr} g/L for this postnatal week and respiratory support (Kirpalani, NEJM 2020).
flag.spo2_sao2_gap.text: sO₂ and SpO₂ differ by {gap}%: check the sample type, the pulse oximeter probe and dyshaemoglobins.
flag.cohb_elevated.text: FCOHb {v}%: above the non-smoker normal (< 3%). Up to 10% is possible in smokers.
flag.cohb_neonate.text: FCOHb {v}%: in a neonate this may indicate haemolysis (including isoimmune).
flag.cohb_poisoning.text: FCOHb {v}% (> 10%): carbon monoxide poisoning is likely — 100% O₂, assess neurology and heart.
flag.cohb_hbo.text: FCOHb {v}% (> 25%; > 15–20% in pregnancy): consider hyperbaric oxygen (ACEP, UHMS).
flag.methb_elevated.text: FMetHb {v}% (normal < 2%). Neonates are at higher risk (low cytochrome-b5 reductase, diarrhoea, acidosis).
flag.methb_cyanosis.text: FMetHb {v}% (> 10%): cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen is possible. Find the cause (nitrates, drugs).
flag.methb_symptomatic.text: FMetHb {v}%: if symptomatic — methylene blue 1–2 mg/kg IV over 5 min (neonates 0.3–1 mg/kg); contraindicated in G6PD deficiency.
flag.methb_treat.text: FMetHb {v}% (> 30%): methylene blue is indicated regardless of symptoms (except G6PD deficiency).
flag.hypokalemia_mild.text: K⁺ {K} mmol/L (3.0–3.4): mild hypokalaemia. Check Mg²⁺; in alkalosis part of K⁺ has shifted into cells.
flag.hypokalemia_severe.text: K⁺ {K} mmol/L (< 2.5): severe hypokalaemia — risk of arrhythmia, ECG monitoring.
flag.hyperkalemia_mild.text: K⁺ {K} mmol/L (5.5–5.9). Rule out a haemolysed sample (especially capillary and neonatal).
flag.hyperkalemia_severe.text: K⁺ {K} mmol/L (≥ 6.5): severe hyperkalaemia — emergency protocol (membrane stabilisation with calcium, shift K⁺ into cells).
flag.hypocalcemia_mild.text: Ionised Ca²⁺ {ca} mmol/L (normal 1.15–1.30). Use the actual cCa²⁺, not cCa²⁺(7.4).
flag.hypocalcemia.text: Ionised Ca²⁺ {ca} mmol/L: hypocalcaemia (children and adults < 1.0; term neonates < 1.1). Alkalosis lowers Ca²⁺ further.
flag.hypocalcemia_severe.text: Ionised Ca²⁺ {ca} mmol/L (< 0.8): severe hypocalcaemia — ECG, correction with calcium gluconate.
flag.hypocalcemia_preterm.text: Ionised Ca²⁺ {ca} mmol/L: in a stable preterm infant treat usually below 0.8; if unstable, below 1.1 (RCH Melbourne).
flag.glucose_neo_iv.text: Glucose {g} mmol/L in a neonate (< 1.0): intravenous treatment (BAPM 2017).
flag.glucose_neo_low.text: Glucose {g} mmol/L (< 2.0): hypoglycaemia — act according to protocol (BAPM 2017; treat below 2.5 if symptomatic).
flag.glucose_neo_target.text: Glucose {g} mmol/L is below the target {t} mmol/L (PES 2015: > 2.8 in the first 48 h, > 3.3 afterwards).
flag.glucose_neo_high.text: Glucose {g} mmol/L (> 8.3): check the glucose infusion rate.
flag.glucose_neo_insulin.text: Glucose {g} mmol/L (> 14): reduce the glucose infusion rate; if it persists, consider insulin (NICE NG154).
flag.hypoglycemia_severe.text: Glucose {g} mmol/L (< 3.0): level 2 hypoglycaemia — correct immediately.
flag.dka_criteria.text: Glucose {g} mmol/L (> 11) with pH < 7.3 or HCO₃⁻ < 18: check ketones — DKA criteria (ISPAD 2022).
flag.glucose_icu_high.text: Glucose {g} mmol/L (> 10): ICU target 7.8–10, insulin above 10 (NICE-SUGAR, ADA).
flag.lactate_severe.text: Lactate {l} mmol/L (≥ 4): high risk; in sepsis a sign of shock (SSC 2021).
flag.lactate_neo.text: Lactate {l} mmol/L: above what is expected for age (up to ~4 in the first 6 h, then < 2.5). Assess perfusion; if persistent, consider inborn errors of metabolism.
flag.lactate_cord.text: Cord lactate {l} mmol/L (> 6.2): associated with neurological abnormality — assess for encephalopathy.
flag.bili_exchange.text: Bilirubin {b} µmol/L is at the exchange transfusion threshold for gestational age ({ex} µmol/L; phototherapy {photo}; Maisels 2012).
flag.bili_photo.text: Bilirubin {b} µmol/L is above the phototherapy threshold for gestational age ({photo} µmol/L; exchange {ex}; Maisels 2012). With risk factors use the lower end.
flag.bili_below_preterm.text: Bilirubin {b} µmol/L is below the phototherapy threshold for gestational age ({photo} µmol/L; Maisels 2012).
flag.bili_aap.text: Bilirubin {b} µmol/L at {h} h: for ≥ 35 weeks check the hour-specific AAP 2022 nomogram (bilitool.org), accounting for neurotoxicity risk factors.
treat.k.title: Potassium (KCl) — educational calculation
treat.k.ratePed: Rate no more than {rate} mmol/h (0.2 mmol/kg/h; up to {icu} mmol/h only in ICU with ECG monitoring) — over at least {h} h
treat.k.rateAdult: Rate no more than {rate} mmol/h peripherally, up to {icu} mmol/h centrally with ECG monitoring
treat.k.conc: Concentration no more than {p} mmol/L (peripheral) and {c} mmol/L (central line)
treat.k.notes: Check Mg²⁺ and urine output; in alkalosis K⁺ has partly shifted into cells — recheck 1–2 h after correction.
treat.ca.title: Calcium gluconate 10% — educational calculation
treat.ca.dosePed: {ml} mL (0.5 mL/kg = 50 mg/kg, max 20 mL) IV over 5–10 min
treat.ca.notes: Under ECG monitoring; do not mix with bicarbonate or phosphate in the same line; watch for extravasation.
flag.hypoxemia.text: PaO₂ {PaO2} mmHg is below the age-specific normal ({lo}).
flag.hypoxemia_severe.text: PaO₂ {PaO2} mmHg (< 60) on FiO₂ {FiO2}: marked hypoxaemia — confirm the sample is arterial and assess the cause (shunt, V/Q).
work.label: Calculation
work.bicarb: Deficit = {f} × {w} kg × |{BE}| = {def} mmol; first dose ½ = {dose} mmol; volume = {dose} / {c} mmol/mL = {vol} mL
work.kPed: Dose = 0.5 mmol/kg × {w} kg = {dose} mmol; rate ≤ 0.2 mmol/kg/h × {w} kg = {rate} mmol/h; time ≥ {dose} / {rate} = {h} h
work.kAdult: Dose {dose} mmol at ≤ {rate} mmol/h → time ≥ {dose} / {rate} = {h} h
work.caPed: 0.5 mL/kg × {w} kg = {ml} mL of 10% solution (= {mg} mg calcium gluconate)
work.sodium: TBW = {f} × {w} kg = {tbw} L; Na⁺ deficit = {tbw} × ({target} − {Na}) = {v} mmol; first 24 h (rise ≤ {max} mmol/L): {first} mmol
work.freeWater: TBW = {f} × {w} kg = {tbw} L; free water deficit = {tbw} × ({Na} / {ref} − 1) = {v} L; first 24 h (Na⁺ fall ≤ {max} mmol/L): {first} L
deficit.title: Deficits — educational calculation
deficit.sodium.title: Sodium (hyponatraemia)
deficit.sodium.note: Raise Na⁺ by no more than {max} mmol/L in 24 h (risk of osmotic demyelination). Recheck Na⁺ every 2–4 h. TBW factor: preterm 0.8, term 0.75, child and man 0.6, woman 0.5.
deficit.freeWater.title: Free water (hypernatraemia)
deficit.freeWater.note: Lower Na⁺ by no more than {max} mmol/L in 24 h (≈ 0.5 mmol/L/h) — risk of cerebral oedema. Add ongoing losses and maintenance needs to the deficit.
deficit.chloride.title: Chloride (chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis)
deficit.chloride.note: Replace with NaCl and/or KCl (KCl first if hypokalaemic). Cl⁻ distribution volume ≈ 0.2 L/kg.
process.title: How the conclusion is reached
process.intro: The analysis runs in a strict order: each step uses the results of the previous ones. A step runs only if its data were entered; the formulas with your numbers are shown in each step below.
process.consistency: are the numbers right: [H⁺] from pH must match [H⁺] from pCO₂ and HCO₃⁻
process.ph: which way pH has shifted from the age-specific normal
process.primary: which value explains the shift — pCO₂ (respiratory) or HCO₃⁻ (metabolic)
process.compensation: does the other value match the expected compensation; if not, there is a second disorder
process.anionGap: are there unmeasured anions (lactate, ketones, toxins); albumin correction
process.deltaRatio: does the rise in AG explain the whole fall in HCO₃⁻, or is there another metabolic disorder
process.osmolar: are there osmotically active substances (toxic alcohols)
process.stewart: which mechanisms make up the SBE (chloride, albumin, lactate, unmeasured anions)
process.oxygenation: how impaired is oxygenation; are there criteria for ARDS, iNO or ECMO
process.labs: what else needs attention: Hb, oximetry, K⁺, Ca²⁺, glucose, lactate, bilirubin — by age norms
process.outro: The conclusion is assembled from the step results: primary disorder, its compensation, additional disorders, then warnings. The correction block is an educational calculation; the physician decides.
chart.map.title: Acid–base map
chart.map.caption: The patient's point on the pCO₂ × HCO₃⁻ plane. Dashed lines are pH isopleths; coloured corridors show expected compensation ±2 (light — acute, solid — chronic); the green box is the age-specific normal.
chart.gamble.title: Gamblegram — anion gap
chart.gamble.caption: Cations equal anions. The difference between Na⁺ and the measured anions (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻) is the unmeasured anions, i.e. the AG.
chart.bili.title: Bilirubin and treatment thresholds
chart.bili.captionMaisels: Gestational age {ga} weeks: Maisels 2012 operational thresholds (lower end of range), µmol/L.
chart.bili.captionAAP: Gestational age {ga} weeks: hour-specific AAP 2022 thresholds, µmol/L.
field.biliRisk: Neurotoxicity risk factors (GA < 38 wk, albumin < 30 g/L, haemolysis, sepsis, instability)
flag.bili_aap_below.text: Bilirubin {b} µmol/L at {h} h is below the AAP 2022 phototherapy threshold ({photo} µmol/L).
flag.bili_aap_photo.text: Bilirubin {b} µmol/L at {h} h is above the AAP 2022 phototherapy threshold ({photo} µmol/L; exchange {ex}).
flag.bili_aap_escalation.text: Bilirubin {b} µmol/L at {h} h is within 34 µmol/L of the exchange threshold ({ex}): escalation of care per AAP 2022.
flag.bili_aap_exchange.text: Bilirubin {b} µmol/L at {h} h is at the AAP 2022 exchange threshold ({ex} µmol/L).
metric.title: Detailed assessment
metric.caption: Derived values with formula, normal range and verdict. Some match the ABL analyzer's calculated parameters (cBase(Ecf), cCa²⁺(7.4), pH(T), pCO₂(T), FShunt, pO₂(a/A), RI).
metric.agExpected: Expected AG for the albumin level
metric.lactateShare: Share of AG rise explained by lactate
flag.sbe_mismatch.short: BE does not match the calculation
flag.sbe_mismatch.text: Entered BE {be} differs from the calculated SBE {calc} by more than 3: check that cBase(Ecf), not cBase(B), was entered and that the input is correct.
flag.sig_high.text: Strong ion gap {v} mmol/L (> 2): unmeasured anions are present (ketones, toxins, renal failure).
flag.shunt_high.text: Estimated shunt {v}% (normal < 10%): intrapulmonary shunt or V/Q mismatch — consider recruitment, PEEP, chest X-ray.
flag.dead_space_high.text: Vd/Vt {v} (> 0.6): high dead space — associated with high mortality in ARDS (Nuckton 2002).
flag.ba_ratio_high.text: Bilirubin/albumin ratio {v} ≥ {thr}: together with the bilirubin level, exchange transfusion is considered (AAP).
metric.sO2Predicted: Expected sO₂ from the dissociation curve
work.x.p50: {std} × {pO2} / pO₂std(sO₂ {sO2}%) = {v}; normal 24–29 (right shift — acidosis, fever, 2,3-DPG; left — alkalosis, HbF, hypothermia)
flag.so2_mismatch.text: Measured sO₂ {meas}% differs from the value expected from the dissociation curve ({pred}%) by more than 8%: consider dyshaemoglobins, HbF, an air bubble, delayed analysis or an entry error.
deficit.bicarbHCO3.title: Bicarbonate — second estimate (by HCO₃⁻)
deficit.bicarbHCO3.note: The HCO₃⁻ distribution volume grows in severe acidosis (0.5 → 0.8 L/kg). Compare with the BE-based calculation in the correction block; usually half the deficit is given and the gas repeated.
deficit.maintenance.title: Maintenance fluid requirement
deficit.maintenance.note: 4 mL/kg/h for the first 10 kg, 2 mL/kg/h for the next 10 kg, 1 mL/kg/h for each kg above 20. Deficits and ongoing losses are added to this volume.
chart.odc.title: Oxygen–haemoglobin dissociation curve
chart.odc.caption: Dashed — standard curve (pH 7.4, pCO₂ 40, 37 °C). Solid — the curve at the patient's pH, pCO₂ and temperature (Bohr effect). Dot — measured pO₂ and sO₂; verticals — p50.
chart.cascade.title: Oxygen cascade
chart.cascade.caption: pO₂ falls from inspired gas (PIO₂) to the alveoli (PAO₂) and to arterial blood (PaO₂). A large drop between PAO₂ and PaO₂ (A-a) means shunt, V/Q mismatch or a diffusion barrier.
chart.profile.title: Deviation profile
chart.profile.caption: Every entered value on one scale: the green band is the age-specific normal, right is above normal, left is below. Colour: green — normal, amber — moderate deviation, red — marked.
chart.profile.aria: Deviation profile of values from normal
